dimensions.reason: A mutual fund-backed savings account for 'idle savings' suits working adults with surplus cash; no age data published.
Bengaluru startup selling liquid-fund yield over bank savings, a concept that resonates with financially literate urban users.
Targets people with balances sitting idle; plans for current-account and MSME offerings add business owners.
The Paypers says the real-time redemption feature caters to 'high-net-worth individuals seeking efficient treasury management'.
Mutual fund investing in India skews male; no Curie data published. Weak.

caveats: App only went live for all users in October 2025; user base is small and undisclosed.

LivQuik.headline: Employees, fleet drivers and commuters using QuikWallet for employer-loaded expense wallets, meal cards, FASTag and NCMC

dimensions.reason: Main uses are employee expense wallets, meal cards and FASTag, held by working adults; site also lists teen and elderly segments.
Meal cards, corporate expense and NCMC metro cards concentrate in large cities; highway FASTag adds fleets elsewhere.
App lets businesses 'load funds into employee wallets remotely'; a fleet operator testimonial cites its 'fleet customers'.
Corporate meal-card and expense-wallet holders are typically formally employed middle earners.
Fleet, field-expense and FASTag users skew male; no data published.

caveats: LivQuik is mainly a B2B prepaid issuance stack for fintechs; QuikWallet is its own consumer app.
